whys: Platform, Android and the dates remain whole, making the matrix easy to scan. The merged release note is narrow and tall, with several awkward breaks in Chinese words, which makes the middle rows feel stretched.
Platform names and dates remain whole and easy to scan. The narrow v3.3 area makes the merged release note tall and splits Chinese phrases across lines, but the table remains clear.
Platform names and dates remain whole and easy to scan. The merged release note is narrow and tall, with some awkward Chinese line breaks, making the middle rows spacious.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: Equal widths leave too little room for the Platform and Android labels, forcing breaks in the row-header column while giving extra space to short date fields.
candidates.label: acceptable

whys: The dates remain whole, but Platform and Android both break inside the word. Those prominent splits interrupt row and column identification, while the merged note also has awkward breaks.
Dates stay on one line, but Platform and Android break within words, weakening the row and column labels used for navigation. The uneven row heights also interrupt the table’s rhythm.
Dates remain whole, but Platform and Android break inside the words. Those prominent breaks impede row identification and give the first column an uneven appearance.

The headers and platform names remain whole, and the merged note has a more comfortable measure. However, all four v3.2 dates split across two lines, making an important set of values harder to scan and compare.
Labels and the merged release note fit comfortably, with balanced row heights. However, all four v3.2 dates break after the hyphen, making the date columns harder to scan and compare.
Platform names and the merged release note fit more comfortably, but all four v3.2 dates break across two lines. That makes the principal date comparisons slower and disrupts the matrix.

d1.purpose: 按平台和版本阶段查阅发布状态或日期，并比较不同平台的发布安排。
tasks: 从平台行定位对应的版本与 Beta、GA 阶段。
比较 iOS 与 Android 的日期，并识别跨平台同步发布的说明。
沿版本顺序阅读各平台的发布安排，区分 Web 的持续部署与移动端的版本发布。
relations: v3.2 和 v3.3 各统领 Beta、GA 两列。
v3.3 的跨行跨列说明同时适用于 iOS 和 Android 的两个阶段。
Web 的持续部署说明跨越 v3.2 的两个阶段。
roles: 首列是平台行标题，需支持快速纵向定位。
上层列标题区分版本，下层列标题区分发布阶段。
日期用于比较；合并单元格中的文字解释适用于多个阶段或平台的共同状态。
keep_whole: 日期及其他不可拆分的英文或数字标识
may_wrap: 合并单元格中的中文说明可在自然语义位置换行。
中英文混排说明换行时应尽量保持英文词语和名称完整。
same_scale: 同一版本下的 Beta 与 GA 列宜保持接近的尺度，便于按阶段比较。
四个阶段标题具有相同层级，但列宽可根据日期和合并说明的需求区别分配。
d1.h_vs_v: 333px 的宽度不足以让所有单列内容都按最宽单行尺寸显示。适度增加行高可为日期和合并说明争取可读空间；跨列说明可利用两列的总宽，而其跨行结构也使高度分配影响两个平台行。

d2.purpose: 呈现各平台在 v3.2 和 v3.3 中的发布状态与安排。
tasks: 按平台和版本查找 Beta 或 GA 的发布信息。
比较 iOS 与 Android 的日期，识别跨版本阶段或跨平台共用的说明。
查看 Web 的持续部署方式。
relations: Beta 和 GA 分属于各自的版本标题。
v3.3 的合并说明同时适用于 iOS 和 Android 的两个阶段。
Web 在 v3.2 下的说明横跨两个阶段。
roles: 首列是跨两行表头的平台索引，也是各数据行的行标题。
上层表头区分版本，下层表头区分 Beta 与 GA。
日期用于比较；合并单元格中的文字说明共同适用的发布安排。
keep_whole: 日期和 App Store 等名称宜保持完整。
may_wrap: 中文发布说明可在自然语义边界换行。
中英文混排说明可在中文短句之间换行，避免拆开英文名称。
same_scale: 同级的 Beta 和 GA 列应有可比较的视觉尺度，但可因日期和合并说明的空间需求而不同。
两个版本组应清楚对应各自的子列，不必等宽。
d2.h_vs_v: 333px 的视口不足以让所有说明保持单行。首列先保证平台名称完整，其余空间在日期的完整性与合并说明的自然换行之间分配；增加说明区域宽度可减少行高，但会压缩其他列。

d3.purpose: 展示不同平台在 v3.2 和 v3.3 发布阶段的状态与日期。
tasks: 按平台查找 Beta 和 GA 的发布日期或发布状态。
比较同一平台的不同阶段，以及不同平台之间的发布安排。
识别跨平台共享的说明和 Web 的持续部署方式。
relations: v3.2 和 v3.3 各包含 Beta 与 GA 两个阶段。
v3.3 的合并说明同时适用于 iOS 和 Android，且跨越两个阶段。
Web 在 v3.2 下的持续部署说明跨越两个阶段；v3.3 下以破折号表示。
roles: 第一列是平台行标题，用于定位和区分 iOS、Android 与 Web。
上层表头按版本分组，下层表头标识发布阶段。
日期是需要快速比较的数据；合并单元格中的文字是对发布方式或状态的说明。
keep_whole: App Store 等英文名称应尽量保持完整
may_wrap: 中文发布说明可在自然语义边界换行，标点应随相邻文字自然排布。
跨列的持续部署说明可换行，但应保持语句连续。
same_scale: 四个发布阶段列应保持可比较的视觉尺度，同时可依据合并说明的空间需求有所区别。
平台标签共用一个足以完整容纳最长标签的列宽。
d3.h_vs_v: 总宽度受限时，优先保证平台名、阶段名和日期完整；将余宽分配给跨列说明，以减少中文和英文名称的不自然换行。允许说明增加行数，以换取清晰的列结构。

analysis.strengths: Fits the viewport exactly. Both header levels stay on one line, as do the platform names and dates. The merged release note is readable and remains visually associated with both mobile platforms.
analysis.faults: The release note is six lines tall, making the two mobile rows unusually deep. Some Chinese words break across lines, and the Web note wraps onto a second line. The table has no spare width.
analysis.spatial_logic: The first column gets 83 px for Platform, the three date-bearing columns get 65 px each, and the remaining 54 px goes to v3.3 Beta. This preserves the one-line headers and dates while giving the merged v3.3 note the space left over.

rounds.insights: The merged notes compete for width with short headers and dates that are useful to scan intact. At this viewport, the measured widths leave essentially no room to enlarge either merged region without making a platform name, header, or date wrap. The tall mobile rows are a reasonable cost for preserving those lookup cues.

contrast.why: Equal widths leave too little room for the Platform and Android labels, forcing breaks in the row-header column while giving extra space to short date fields.

sameFunctionGroups.why: These are parallel release-status columns. A broadly consistent scale helps comparison, though the merged cells and the shorter content in column 4 justify the small width difference in P.

synthesis.rationale: P fits the viewport and keeps the platform names, dates, version headings, App Store and Google Play legible. Its merged release note occupies six lines but remains easy to associate with both iOS and Android. The narrow text measure does split some Chinese words across lines, a compromise imposed by the fixed padding and viewport.

general: Protect identifiers, dates and row labels from disruptive breaks before distributing space evenly.
Judge merged cells by their combined width and the reading relationship they create.
Use a consistent scale for parallel columns when their contents and spanning cells allow it.
specific: The first column needs 83 px to accommodate Platform and Android with the fixed padding.
The two v3.3 columns together need enough width to make the shared release note readable.

synthesis.tradeoffs: P uses the full available width and preserves the main lookup fields, at the cost of a tall shared note and several Chinese word breaks.
synthesis.uncertain: Only P was supplied, so its selection does not establish that it is the best possible width allocation. The measured word-break count does not by itself show how disruptive each break is in context.

critique.cause: v3.3 GA 列宽 54px，日期的可用文本宽度不足；v3.3 合并区域总宽 119px，限制了说明的自然换行。

contrast.idea: Equal widths leave too little room for the Platform and Android labels, forcing breaks in the row-header column while giving extra space to short date fields.

d1r1A.why: Platform, Android and the dates remain whole, making the matrix easy to scan. The merged release note is narrow and tall, with several awkward breaks in Chinese words, which makes the middle rows feel stretched.

contrast.why: The dates remain whole, but Platform and Android both break inside the word. Those prominent splits interrupt row and column identification, while the merged note also has awkward breaks.

ref_auto.why: The headers and platform names remain whole, and the merged note has a more comfortable measure. However, all four v3.2 dates split across two lines, making an important set of values harder to scan and compare.

acceptance.unsure: The choice depends on the reading task: C has a more compact, even shape and no measured word breaks, but its split dates are a substantial lookup cost. A preserves those dates at the expense of a taller, more fragmented release note.

d1r1A.why: Platform names and dates remain whole and easy to scan. The narrow v3.3 area makes the merged release note tall and splits Chinese phrases across lines, but the table remains clear.

contrast.why: Dates stay on one line, but Platform and Android break within words, weakening the row and column labels used for navigation. The uneven row heights also interrupt the table’s rhythm.

ref_auto.why: Labels and the merged release note fit comfortably, with balanced row heights. However, all four v3.2 dates break after the hyphen, making the date columns harder to scan and compare.

acceptance.unsure: The relative weight of A’s longer Chinese note versus C’s split dates depends on whether readers primarily scan release dates or read the shared release note.

d1r1A.why: Platform names and dates remain whole and easy to scan. The merged release note is narrow and tall, with some awkward Chinese line breaks, making the middle rows spacious.

contrast.why: Dates remain whole, but Platform and Android break inside the words. Those prominent breaks impede row identification and give the first column an uneven appearance.

ref_auto.why: Platform names and the merged release note fit more comfortably, but all four v3.2 dates break across two lines. That makes the principal date comparisons slower and disrupts the matrix.

acceptance.unsure: The measured word-break count does not capture how disruptive the date breaks in C are; the ranking gives substantial weight to scanning and comparing those dates.
